# Fable 5.1 final review before v0.1.0

Verdict: fix first

Reviewed at HEAD c7dbf0f on nikita/feat/scribe-bootstrap, 2026-09-09. Read-only: no source, test, record or git state touched; only this file written. Line numbers are HEAD. Every "fails on the old code" claim below was checked by reading the test against the pre-fix diff, and the four new defects were reproduced by running code, not by reasoning alone.

## Batch A group 3

- V5: closed. `check._validate_all_records` (check.py:99) validates every current record; `_attestation_integrity` (check.py:137) and `store.attestation_line_problems` (store.py:125) report malformed, incomplete and truncated lines; `ratify._ledger_broken` (ratify.py:78) refuses to append. `test_appending_a_contradictory_attestation_fails_an_unchanged_record` fails on the old code, which validated only files the diff touched. `test_ratify_refuses_to_append_after_a_truncated_ledger_tail` asserts the ledger is byte-identical to before plus the truncated line; the old unconditional append glues a new line onto it. Residual, acceptable: `Store.latest_attestation` still accepts an incomplete line as authority for `effective_authority`, but `scribe check` fails that ledger anyway.
- V6: closed. `_deleted_record_reasons` (check.py:163) compares `ls-tree` at the fork point against HEAD; three tests, and the old code had no rule at all. No escape hatch, as the owner asked. Rename counts as delete plus `alias_filename_mismatch` (I95), fine.
- V14: closed. `_paths_from_z` (gitutil.py:16) with `-z` on all five helpers; `tests/test_gitutil.py` uses a real repository with cafe, tab and quote filenames. The old backslash-to-slash replace corrupts the octal escapes git emits for the non-ASCII name.
- V17: closed. `_in_str_set` (schema.py:338) on every enum, `ulid_date_out_of_range` (schema.py:274-289), `Store.records` skips and logs one bad file (store.py:46). The three tests raise TypeError, ValueError and FrontMatterError respectively on the old code.

## Batch B

- V12: closed for the gate, with one regression (New defects 3). `Store.effective_authority` (store.py:111) requires the latest attestation ratified with a matching body hash, `review_state` ratified, `effective_state` proposed or implemented, and no effective incoming edge. `test_action_authority_requires_live_matching_attestation` (unattested, expired, superseded, body hash) fails on the old review_state-only check. `reconcile.task_completed` keeps the flag under enforce (reconcile.py:80) and `test_task_completed_enforce_exits_two` asserts it. Behaviour change nobody wrote down, not a defect: `commit_msg.active_records` (commit_msg.py:94) now warns about governed paths only for ratified records, so an unreviewed implemented record no longer nudges a commit to link to it.
- V3: partial, as the owner scoped it. Dirty guard (`gitutil.is_dirty`, gitutil.py:41; `run_check`, check.py:226) and base-tip question (`_supersede_gate`, check.py:85) are done; `test_a_ratification_added_to_the_target_after_the_fork_is_honoured` fails on the merge-base version. Missing: (a) the revision-backed store is deferred with no record, unlike V7, V13 and V23; (b) Codex's "git range failures must produce explicit check failures" is untouched: `diff_names`, `rev_list_range` and `tree_record_paths` return `[]` on a git error and a `merge_base` failure silently falls back to `base` (check.py:192), so a bad ref or a shallow CI clone can make the historical rules pass vacuously. Cost already logged in M14: `scribe check` refuses right after every implementing commit because post-commit leaves docs/decisions dirty.
- V8: closed, with one regression (New defects 2). One lock (`state.ledger_lock_path`) in new, post-commit, relink, lint --expire and ratify; exclusive create in `_write_record_exclusive` (newrecord.py:158); reload after acquire everywhere. Five timeout tests hold a real flock past 2 s, and the old code took no lock. Lock analysis: no code path acquires the ledger lock twice in one process (state.json.lock is a different file, taken inside post-commit and new only after the ledger lock); a nested acquire would block for 2 s because `locked` opens a second handle, and none exists. post-commit and post-rewrite are sequential hook processes, never nested, so an amend under contention costs at most 2 s plus 2 s and writes nothing.
- V19: closed. `push_recent(cap=None)` (state.py:232), `_register` (newrecord.py:313); `test_pending_decisions_has_no_cap_and_all_survive_as_trailer_candidates` registers 25 ids where the old code kept 20.
- V21: closed as scoped (warn only). `session_start.subdirectory_hint` (session_start.py:33) and the init follow-up (init_repo.py:332); the hint test fails on the old handler, which returned None for an empty queue regardless of cwd.

## 08-review follow-ups

- P2 state-lock false deny: partial. The fix is right: `plan_verdict` reads `pending` from the state `update_state` returns (pre_tool_use_gate.py:105-108) and `update_state` returns `load_state` on timeout (state.py:205). No regression test: `grep -i lock tests/test_hook_gate.py` is empty; contention is only tested at the state layer.
- P2 rm boundary: regressed. The reported input (`rm build`, newline, `printf ... -rf /tmp/example`) is fixed by `matching_rules` splitting on newlines (policy.py:145), but the split ignores backslash continuation, so every rule now misses a continued command. Reproduced: `git push origin main \` newline `  --force` gives `[]`; `rm -rf \` newline ` /tmp/x` gives `[]`; the old whitespace collapse matched both. Generated multi-line shell commands use continuation routinely. Fix: join `\\\r?\n` before splitting, add both cases to `test_denylist_matches`.
- V1 supervisor: partial. The tokened marker (supervise.py:40-49, protocol.py:19) and the forced exit 2 or 1 (supervise.py:58) close the two protocol gaps; `test_marker_forces_blocking_status` fails on the old pass-through. But `test_traceback_marker_impersonation_is_fail_open` (test_supervise.py:176) does not test the fix: its fake uv prints `RuntimeError: [scribe-deny]` on one line, and the old whole-line comparison already ignored that; only a bare `[scribe-deny]` line fooled the old code. Print the bare line so the test bites. `-I -S` on hooks.json is right; the git shim re-execs itself under `-I -S` (githook_shim.py:14-18) but the first interpreter start still honours the user's `PYTHONHOME`, which is exactly the case Codex raised. Unfixable from a shebang shim; worth one README sentence.

## Pytest verify engine

Schema (`_validate_pytest_target`, schema.py:478) and runner (`_run_pytest_verify_entry`, lint.py:480) are sound on the happy path: argv list, no shell, `cwd=store.root`, bounded timeout, exit 0 and 1 mapped, everything else `verify_error`. Timeout handling checked empirically: the 1 s timeout test against a 5 s sleep finishes in 3.4 s, so uv does not leave an orphaned pytest holding the pipes.

Defect (New defects 4): lint executes entries the validator rejects. `_verify_findings` (lint.py:361) dispatches on `engine` alone and the runner checks only "non-empty string" (lint.py:496). Reproduced: `target: "--version"` makes the validator say `invalid_verify: verify target path does not exist` while the runner returns `[]`, because `pytest --version` exits 0 and counts as passed. Same for a `..` path or an absolute path. A record is committed content, so this is not privilege escalation, but the option-injection surface (`-p`, `-o addopts=`, `--rootdir`) is real and `expect: pass` on a non-test target passes silently. Fix: call `_validate_pytest_target` in the runner, or skip verify entries on records that carry validation errors. Minor: the subprocess leaves `.pytest_cache` in the linted repo; pass `-p no:cacheprovider`.

## Post-rewrite hook

`post_rewrite.run` (post_rewrite.py:48) drains stdin, reuses `run_relink`, maps its lock timeout to exit 0. The re-entry guard is set in the hook's own process only and is never inherited, so it cannot trigger; same as post_commit's, harmless. Amend flow verified by test: post-commit adds the new sha, post-rewrite drops the old one, `test_amend_keeps_one_trailer_and_relinks_to_the_new_sha` asserts exactly one link and one `relinked` event. Rebase: `test_rebase_onto_end_to_end_leaves_both_records_linked_to_new_shas` runs a real `rebase --onto` with all four hooks live. I127 is real and pre-existing: post-commit fires per replayed commit, writes unstaged backlinks, and a later commit in the same range touching docs/decisions conflicts; the proposal record covers it. Lock: sequential with post-commit, no nesting, fail-open on timeout (`test_post_rewrite_lock_timeout_fails_open_without_writing`). No defect found beyond I127.

## The four new records

- D-260909-history-replay-validation-every-changed (V7): ratify. A real decision with a dated review, three options with the strawman labelled as such. Evidence "Go ahead" is the owner's approval of the triage order, not of V7 by name; acceptable because the pointer names the triage document that lists V7 under Batch C.
- D-260909-the-git-hooks-keep-reading-records-and-a (V13): rewrite. The Decision claims "The module docstring of commit_msg.py states this (V13, staged content not inspected)"; the docstring mentions only F13 verify entries, never V13 or working-tree reads (commit_msg.py:1-7). The verify entry greps "staged content" and matches that unrelated F13 sentence, so it proves nothing. Constraints and Requires say README marks commit-msg enforce "not yet recommended"; README lines 145-150 describe enforce with no caveat. Make the two doc changes in the same commit or drop the claims.
- D-260909-tests-keep-copying-the-live-docs-decisio (V23): ratify. The Decision matches conftest.py (`SEED_RECORD_ALIASES`) and is linked to 27aefbe. Two honest wrinkles: the title says the rewrite waits for "the first unrelated breakage" while the body says that breakage already happened and pinning absorbed it; criterion 2 (the suite must not modify the checkout) is knowingly unmet by the chosen option.
- D-260909-post-commit-skips-its-backlink-write-whi (rebase proposal): hold, rewrite before ratifying. The design is right (skip when `rebase-merge` or `rebase-apply` exists, let post-rewrite relink once) and the options are honest. But the Evidence blockquote "(no user turn; self-initiated)" is a placeholder that satisfies `missing_evidence_quote` by pretending to be a quote, and `decided_by: agent` describes a decision nobody has made. Once the owner answers, that turn belongs in the quote. The seed record's regret line is more than 1 in 5 records without a decisive turn; this batch is 1 in 4.

Alias truncation mid-word (M12) leaves two of the four aliases unreadable; cosmetic, already logged.

## New defects

1. Denylist bypass on line continuation, introduced by 3050f09 (policy.py:145). Reproduction above. The gate is the only enforcement surface, and false allows also corrupt the shadow-mode measurement the owner is collecting.
2. `scribe new` writes records with the execute bit, introduced by 406cced. `_write_record_exclusive` (newrecord.py:177) calls `os.open(path, O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_WRONLY)` with the default mode 0o777, so records land as 0775. Verified: `ls -l docs/decisions` shows `rwxrwxr-x` on three of the four new records and `git ls-tree HEAD` shows 100755 for them; c7dbf0f already carries a 100755 to 100644 flip for the fourth because `Record.save` rewrites through a temp file. Fix: pass `0o644`; chmod the three committed records before tagging so the ledger does not carry one mode flip per record on first save.
3. INDEX.md drops a ratified backtracked record, introduced by 3050f09. In `render_index` (index.py:162-168) `_retired_state` returns None for backtracked and `effective_authority` requires proposed or implemented, so the record lands in neither section. Reproduced in a temp copy: alias absent, Active drops from 3 to 2. Before the change `ACTIVE_STATES` included backtracked. List backtracked under Retired, or widen the predicate; `tests/test_index.py` never mentions backtracked.
4. Lint executes verify targets the validator rejects (lint.py:361, 496). Reproduction above.
5. Duplicate `Decision:` trailer on 27aefbe: alias-only from the commit message, alias plus ULID from prepare-commit-msg. `add_trailer_to_file` (gitutil.py:187) uses `addIfDifferent` on the whole value; `prepare_commit_msg.run` (prepare_commit_msg.py:108) should treat an existing trailer whose tokens resolve to the same record as present. Cosmetic; lookup and relink resolve both forms.
6. `test_traceback_marker_impersonation_is_fail_open` does not exercise the token fix (see 08-review follow-ups).
7. No regression test for the plan-gate lock contention fix (P2).

Not repeated as defects: V7 replay, V13 staged content, V23 fixtures.
